{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Fish|Fish]]

This '''fried fish''' is battered and [[Cookbook:Deep frying|deep-fat fried]]. You'll need thin fish filets that don't fall apart when cooked. Fried fish go well with [[Cookbook:Soda Pop|soda]] and can be served with [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]], [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]], or a mixture of the two. They could also be served with [[Cookbook:Sweet and Sour|sweet-and-sour]] sauce or [[Cookbook:Teriyaki Sauce|teriyaki]] sauce.

==Ingredients==

* [[Cookbook:Oil|Oil]] with a high smoke point
* Thin [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] fillets (e.g. [[Cookbook:Catfish|catfish]], [[Cookbook:Tilapia|tilapia]], or the less-durable [[Cookbook:Flounder|flounder]])
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]] white
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Beer|beer]] or 1 cup cold water plus ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* Extra flour to dust the fish

==Procedure==
#Start heating the oil in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]]. This recipe is intended for fast cooking in very hot oil.
#[[Cookbook:Microwave|Microwave]] the fish to ensure that the inside is hot. Flip the fish as you microwave it. When done, the fish should be hot and should look half-cooked.
#Mix the flour, egg white, and beer to make a [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]].
#Pat the fish dry with a [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towel]], then lightly dust it with flour to ensure that it is really dry.
#Dip the fish into the batter, and coat them well. The batter will help protect your hand from splatter.
#Hold the fish right above the oil, then gently slide the fish into the oil.
#With [[Cookbook:Tongs|tongs]], nudge the fish as needed to keep it from sticking to the bottom. Turn the fish over as it cooks.
#Remove the fish when it looks good, then serve it immediately.

==Warnings==

* When a pot of hot oil catches fire, the flames will reach up for 2 or 3 feet. If you must work under flammable cabinets or shelves, be sure to have a fire extinguisher handy. [[Cookbook:Soybean Oil|Soybean oil]], [[Cookbook:Shortening|shortening]], and [[Cookbook:Peanut Oil|peanut oil]] withstand heat better than most cooking oils.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Whip the egg white, or leave it out entirely.
* Add [[Cookbook:Cornmeal|cornmeal]] to the batter.
